title: Triangulated Karoubi envelope
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category. With the shift
$(K,e)[1]=(K[1],e[1])$ and with distinguished triangles the triangles
isomorphic to direct summands, in the category of triangles, of images of
distinguished triangles of $\mathcal T$, the category $\Kar(\mathcal T)$ of
[def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is an ordinary triangulated category, and the
canonical functor of [def-weil-karoubi-envelope] is exact.

(*Source: the classical Balmer--Schlichting idempotent completion of
triangulated categories; retained here as the auxiliary model used in the
proof of the bounded-t-structure theorem below, after which the envelope is
shown to be redundant; no Stacks Project entry states this form: Stacks' only
entries on idempotents are the definition of a Karoubian preadditive category
(Definition 12.4.1, Tag
[09SG](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SG)), its characterization by
the splitting of idempotents (Lemma 12.4.2, Tag
[09SH](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SH)) and the Karoubianity
criteria of Lemma 12.4.3 (Tag
[05QV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05QV): countable products and
kernels of maps which have a right inverse, or dually countable coproducts
and cokernels of maps which have a left inverse), all in Homological Algebra,
Section 12.4 (Tag [09SF](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09SF)); Chapter
13 contains no idempotent completion of a triangulated category, and the
derived-limit and K-injective entries 08TC, 07KC, 0BK6, 0BK7, 070M, 079P
concern a fixed triangulated category rather than its idempotent completion;
the blueprint adds the description of the distinguished triangles of
$\Kar(\mathcal T)$ as retracts of images of distinguished triangles of
$\mathcal T$.*)

proof.text: Write $\mathcal E=\Kar(\mathcal T)$ and $J:\mathcal T\to\mathcal E$ for [def-weil-karoubi-envelope]. We use ordinary functional composition throughout. Each Hom set is the subgroup of $\Hom_{\mathcal T}(K,L)$ consisting of $u=d u e$; the condition is closed under addition and negatives, and composition is bilinear. The zero object is $(0,0)$, and $(K,e)\oplus(L,d)=(K\oplus L,\operatorname{diag}(e,d))$, with inclusions/projections multiplied by the respective projectors, satisfies the biproduct identities. Thus $\mathcal E$ and $J$ are additive. The shifts are $(K,e)[n]=(K[n],e[n])$ and $u[n]$, with the shift coherence maps induced from those of $\mathcal T$ and restricted by the projectors. Naturality makes these legitimate morphisms of $\mathcal E$; inverse coherence maps restrict in the same way, so the usual coherence equations remain true. In particular $[1]$ is an additive autoequivalence and $J$ commutes with shifts. For $A=(K,e)$ put $A^c=(K,1-e)$. The column $(e,1-e)$ and row $(e,1-e)$ give inverse maps $J K\cong A\oplus A^c$, since $e(1-e)=(1-e)e=0$ and $e+(1-e)=1$.

Let $\mathscr D$ be the triangles of $\mathcal E$ which are retracts of $J\Delta$ for distinguished triangles $\Delta$ of $\mathcal T$: a retract means triangle maps $i:T\to J\Delta$, $p:J\Delta\to T$ with $p i=1_T$. This already includes triangles isomorphic to such retracts, since precomposing $i$ and postcomposing $p$ with inverse triangle isomorphisms preserves $p i=1_T$. It is also closed under further retracts: if $T\overset{a}{\to}T_1\overset{b}{\to}T$ with $b a=1_T$ and $T_1\overset{i}{\to}J\Delta\overset{p}{\to}T_1$ with $p i=1_{T_1}$, then $(i a,b p)$ exhibits $T$ as a retract of $J\Delta$. This is precisely the direct-summand class in the statement, not just a termwise condition: for a retract of $J\Delta$ put $f=i p$, a triangle idempotent with components $f_j$ on the objects $K_j$ of $\Delta$. Its complement has objects $(K_j,1-f_j)$ and arrows $(1-f_{j+1})d_j(1-f_j)$ (with shifted projector at the last target). The commutation equations for $f$ make this a triangle. The componentwise row $(i_j,1-f_j)$ and column $(p_j,1-f_j)$ identify the sum of the retract triangle and this complement with $J\Delta$: the mixed composites vanish since $f i=i$ and $p f=p$, while $i p+(1-f)=1$. Conversely every direct-sum decomposition gives a retract by its inclusion and projection. The contractible triangle of $A$ is a retract of the image of the contractible triangle of $K$ via the triangle projector $(e,e,0)$; its image has identities $e,e$ on its first two terms. This verifies the isomorphism and identity parts of TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category].

To construct cones, first work in $\mathcal T$. Let $\Delta=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$ be distinguished and let $a^2=a$, $b^2=b$, $b u=u a$. TR3 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] gives $x:Z\to Z$ with $x v=v b$ and $w x=a[1]w$. Put $h=x^2-x$. Then $h v=v(b^2-b)=0$ and $w h=(a[1]^2-a[1])w=0$. Clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact], applied with $W=Z$ and $c=h$, gives $h=k w$ for some $k:X[1]\to Z$. Consequently $h^2=k w h=0$. Since $h$ is a polynomial in $x$, it commutes with $x$. Set $r=x+h-2xh=3x^2-2x^3$. Expanding and using $h^2=0$ gives $r^2=x^2+2xh-4x^2h=x+h-2xh=r$, because $x^2=x+h$ and $x^2h=xh$. Also $(r-x)v=(1-2x)hv=0$ and $w(r-x)=wh-2wxh=0$. Hence $(a,b,r)$ is an idempotent endomorphism of $\Delta$. No division by 2 or 3 occurs.

For a morphism $f:(X,a)\to(Y,b)$ in $\mathcal E$, the equation $f=b f a$ gives $b f=f=f a$. Complete its underlying morphism $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal T$ to a distinguished triangle $\Delta=(X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$, using TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], and apply step 3 to $a,b$. The triangle in $\mathcal E$ with objects $(X,a),(Y,b),(Z,r)$ and arrows $f,r v b,a[1]w r$ is a retract of $J\Delta$: inclusion and retraction have underlying components $a,b,r$. For example the second-arrow square reads $r(r v b)=r v b=v b$ and $r v=r v b$, by $r v=v b$; the last-arrow squares follow from $w r=a[1]w$. Their composites on the three objects are $a^2=a$, $b^2=b$, $r^2=r$, the respective identities in the envelope. Thus the triangle belongs to $\mathscr D$ and has first arrow exactly $f$, proving the remaining part of TR1.

Rotation and inverse rotation act on triangle maps and preserve $p i=1$ componentwise. They commute with $J$ under the shift identification of step 1. TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] makes both the rotation and the inverse rotation of a distinguished triangle of $\mathcal T$ distinguished. Applying these operations to a retract diagram therefore proves $T\in\mathscr D\Rightarrow\operatorname{rot}(T)\in\mathscr D$ and $T\in\mathscr D\Rightarrow\operatorname{rot}^{-1}(T)\in\mathscr D$. Applying the latter to $\operatorname{rot}(T)$ and its canonical triangle isomorphism back to $T$ proves the reverse implication required by TR2. The rotated final arrow is $-u[1]$, exactly the convention in the cited definition.

For TR3 let $T,S\in\mathscr D$ with retract diagrams $T\overset{i}{\to}J\Delta\overset{p}{\to}T$ and $S\overset{j}{\to}J\Gamma\overset{q}{\to}S$, and let $(\alpha,\beta)$ be a commuting square on their first arrows. The first two components of $j(\alpha,\beta)p$ form a commuting square between $J\Delta$ and $J\Gamma$. By [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-fully-faithful] they lift to a commuting square in $\mathcal T$, where TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] completes them to a triangle map $t:\Delta\to\Gamma$. Then $q J(t)i:T\to S$ is a triangle map with first components $q_1j_1\alpha p_1i_1=\alpha$ and $q_2j_2\beta p_2i_2=\beta$. This proves TR3 without requiring the chosen third component itself to be idempotent.

Steps 1–6 prove that $(\mathcal E,[1],\mathscr D)$ is pre-triangulated in the precise sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Moreover $J$ is already an exact functor between these pre-triangulated categories: it is additive, has the shift identification from step 1, and $J\Delta$ is its own retract for every distinguished $\Delta$. Only TR4 remains; hence every use below of a theorem for pre-triangulated categories applies without assuming the conclusion we are proving.

Fix composable $u:X\to Y$, $v:Y\to Z$ in $\mathcal E$ and arbitrary distinguished cone triangles $(u,u_1,u_2)$, $(v,v_1,v_2)$, $(vu,w_1,w_2)$, with cones $U,V,W$. Set $A=X^c$, $B=Y^c$, $C=Z^c$ as in step 1. The triangles $A\to0\to A[1]\xrightarrow{1}A[1]$ and $0\to B\xrightarrow{1}B\to0$ are distinguished by TR1 and TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] (rotation of the contractible triangle of $A$ gives final arrow $-1$, and the triangle isomorphism $(1_A,1_0,-1_{A[1]})$ changes it to $1$; inverse rotation of the contractible triangle of $B$ gives the second triangle). Apply [lem-weil-finite-sums-distinguished-triangles] in the pre-triangulated category $\mathcal E$. Adding these trivial triangles to the first cone, and the corresponding triangles for $B,C$ and $A,C$ to the other cones, gives distinguished padded triangles with first two objects $X\oplus A,Y\oplus B,Z\oplus C$ and cones respectively $U\oplus B\oplus A[1]$, $V\oplus C\oplus B[1]$, $W\oplus C\oplus A[1]$. Their first arrows are $\operatorname{diag}(u,0)$, $\operatorname{diag}(v,0)$ and $\operatorname{diag}(vu,0)$, so the third is the composite of the first two. More explicitly, for each of $(s,s_1,s_2;P,Q,D)=(u,u_1,u_2;A,B,U)$, $(v,v_1,v_2;B,C,V)$, and $(vu,w_1,w_2;A,C,W)$, the padded second arrow sends $(y,q)$ to $(s_1y,q,0)$ and its third arrow sends $(d,q,p)$ to $(s_2d,p)$. These expressions denote biproduct maps by their components, rather than elements of the category. Write these arrows as $\bar u_1,\bar u_2$, $\bar v_1,\bar v_2$, and $\bar w_1,\bar w_2$, and write $\bar u=\operatorname{diag}(u,0)$, $\bar v=\operatorname{diag}(v,0)$, $\bar U=U\oplus B\oplus A[1]$, $\bar V=V\oplus C\oplus B[1]$, $\bar W=W\oplus C\oplus A[1]$.

Under $X\oplus A\cong J K_X$, $Y\oplus B\cong J K_Y$, $Z\oplus C\cong J K_Z$ from step 1, the two padded arrows are images of morphisms $K_X\to K_Y\to K_Z$ of $\mathcal T$, by [lem-weil-karoubi-envelope-fully-faithful]. Choose distinguished cone triangles in $\mathcal T$ for these two arrows and their composite using [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Their images in $\mathcal E$ are distinguished by step 7. TR3 completes the chosen isomorphisms on the first two terms of each padded triangle to a triangle morphism from that padded triangle to the corresponding image triangle. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] its third component is an isomorphism. Thus all three padded triangles are isomorphic to images of the three chosen source triangles, with the prescribed isomorphisms on $X\oplus A,Y\oplus B,Z\oplus C$. TR4 in $\mathcal T$ supplies an octahedron for those source triangles. Here are the induced maps and all compatibilities explicitly. Let $a,b,c$ be the fixed isomorphisms on the padded first, second and third base objects, and let $e_U:\bar U\to J U_T$, $e_V:\bar V\to J V_T$, $e_W:\bar W\to J W_T$ be the three cone isomorphisms. Denote the source cone arrows by $u_1^T,u_2^T,v_1^T,v_2^T,w_1^T,w_2^T$, the source base arrows by $u^T,v^T$, and the source front arrows by $F_T:U_T\to W_T$, $G_T:W_T\to V_T$. Set $F=e_W^{-1}J(F_T)e_U$ and $G=e_V^{-1}J(G_T)e_W$. The source octahedron squares and the triangle-isomorphism equations give $e_WF\bar u_1=J(F_T)J(u_1^T)b=J(w_1^T)J(v^T)b=e_W\bar w_1\bar v$, $a[1]\bar w_2F=J(w_2^T)J(F_T)e_U=J(u_2^T)e_U=a[1]\bar u_2$, $e_VG\bar w_1=J(G_T)J(w_1^T)c=J(v_1^T)c=e_V\bar v_1$, and $b[1]\bar v_2G=J(v_2^T)J(G_T)e_W=J(u^T)[1]J(w_2^T)e_W=b[1]\bar u[1]\bar w_2$. Cancelling $e_W,a[1],e_V,b[1]$ gives the four padded octahedron squares. With $H=\bar u_1[1]\bar v_2$, one also has $e_U[1]H=J(u_1^T)[1]b[1]\bar v_2=J(u_1^T[1]v_2^T)e_V$. Therefore $(e_U,e_W,e_V)$ is a triangle isomorphism from $(F,G,H)$ to the image of the source front triangle. That image is distinguished by step 7, so $(F,G,H)$ is distinguished by TR1. All displayed equalities use the shift identification of step 1.

In the following displays, $\operatorname{rows}[a,b,c;d,e,f;g,h,i]$ denotes the matrix with those three rows. Write the two front morphisms of the padded octahedron as $F:U\oplus B\oplus A[1]\to W\oplus C\oplus A[1]$ and $G:W\oplus C\oplus A[1]\to V\oplus C\oplus B[1]$. In block notation the four octahedron squares of [def-weil-triangulated-category] give $F=\operatorname{rows}[f_1,0,f_2;f_3,0,f_4;0,0,1]$ and $G=\operatorname{rows}[g_1,0,g_2;g_3,1,g_4;0,0,0]$; explicitly, $F\bar u_1=\bar w_1\bar v$ on the $B$ summand gives the zero second column of $F$, and $G\bar w_1=\bar v_1$ on the $C$ summand gives the column $(0,1,0)$ of $G$. The $A[1]$-component of $\bar w_2F=\bar u_2$ gives the last row $(0,0,1)$ of $F$, while the $B[1]$-component of $\bar v_2G=\bar u[1]\bar w_2$ gives the zero last row of $G$. The front connecting arrow is $H=\operatorname{rows}[u_1[1]v_2,0,0;0,0,1;0,0,0]$. Projecting those same four squares to the original summands yields $g_1w_1=v_1$, $w_2f_1=u_2$, $f_1u_1=w_1v$, $v_2g_1=u[1]w_2$. The front triangle is distinguished by step 9, so clause (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] gives $GF=0$. Its blocks yield $g_1f_1=0$, $g_1f_2+g_2=0$, $g_3f_1+f_3=0$, and $g_3f_2+f_4+g_4=0$.

On $W\oplus C\oplus A[1]$ set $\sigma=\operatorname{rows}[1,0,-f_2;g_3,1,g_4;0,0,1]$ and $\tau=\operatorname{rows}[1,0,f_2;-g_3,1,f_4;0,0,1]$. Matrix multiplication gives $\sigma\tau=\tau\sigma=1$, since their only potentially nonzero off-diagonal block is $g_3f_2+f_4+g_4=0$. The relations of step 10 also give $\sigma F=\operatorname{rows}[f_1,0,0;0,0,0;0,0,1]$ and $G\tau=\operatorname{rows}[g_1,0,0;0,1,0;0,0,0]$. Replacing the middle object of the front triangle by $\sigma$ thus gives the isomorphic, hence distinguished triangle $(\sigma F,G\tau,H)$ by the isomorphism clause of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. This is an actual change of coordinates; taking the raw first blocks before this change would not give a triangle retract.

The componentwise inclusion of $U,W,V$ into the first summands, and the componentwise projection back, are triangle maps between $(f_1,g_1,u_1[1]v_2)$ and the distinguished triangle of step 11: the three displayed matrices are block diagonal for these summands. Their composite is the identity triangle map. By the retract closure established in step 2, $U\xrightarrow{f_1}W\xrightarrow{g_1}V\xrightarrow{u_1[1]v_2}U[1]$ therefore belongs to $\mathscr D$. The four equalities $g_1w_1=v_1$, $w_2f_1=u_2$, $f_1u_1=w_1v$, $v_2g_1=u[1]w_2$ of step 10 are exactly the four octahedron squares for the original three cone triangles, with this front connecting arrow. This proves TR4 for arbitrary initial cone triangles, as formulated in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Together with steps 1–7 it proves the asserted triangulated structure and exactness of $J$, with exactly the shift and distinguished class in the statement.

lean.note: The recorded module and its public imports Shift and Pretriangulated together give every clause. Karoubi.hasShift has (K,e)[n]=(K[n],e[n]); Karoubi.pretriangulated uses Karoubi.distinguishedTriangles, exactly triangle-category retracts of images of distinguished triangles, as made explicit by Karoubi.mem_distTriang_iff. This class is closed under triangle isomorphisms. Karoubi.isTriangulated proves TR4 for that precise structure. The inclusion is Mathlib's toKaroubi C; toKaroubi.commShift and toKaroubi.isTriangulated give its shift compatibility and exactness. All assumptions are exactly those of an arbitrary triangulated category; there is no boundedness, size equality, or preexisting triangulation hypothesis on the envelope. No new module or repeated statement is needed.
